# P3-A — Lock Screen privacy and disclosure (proof)

**Status:** `P3-A EVIDENCE — NOT FROZEN` (refined: P3-A refinement §5, §6). Evidence: board 10 (all words generated by
`model.project()`), settings boards 07 / 08, checks C-PRIV-1…7 and C-COPY-1, scenarios S28–S31.

## 1. The frozen rules realized (I-08N-01 D14–D17, §10)

- Four levels: **L0 Minimal · L1 Generic · L2 Bounded Context · L3 Content Preview**. The codes are never shown.
- Defaults (D15, verbatim in `DISCLOSURE_DEFAULTS`): Personal / Proactive QANDEEL **L1**; Shared **L2**; Public
  interactions **L2**; Public discovery **L1**; **Introductions L0**; reminders **L2**; System / account **L2**; critical
  security **L2**.
- **L3 is never a default** (C-PRIV-2). Richer disclosure needs the user's explicit choice, per category (D16).
- The user's choice is a **ceiling**: QANDEEL may render less, never more (D17; C-PRIV-3 tries 36 combinations).
- **Event-specific, never category-wide:** an individual event may carry `safeMax` — what that one event's bounded safe
  projection can truthfully carry. It is a fact about the event, not a rule about its category.
- **Critical importance does not raise disclosure** (C-PRIV-4): a new sign-in is L2 even though it is Class 1.
- **Bounded safe projection:** the renderer gets one event's words for one level. No preview can combine Worlds
  (C-PRIV-5).

## 2. Introductions — default L0, no category cap (refinement §5)

The first P3-A pass carried an unapproved rule: "an Introduction never goes beyond L1" (`safeMax: 'L1'` on every
Introductions fixture). **It is removed.** What holds now, exactly as I-08N-01 says:

| | |
|---|---|
| Default | **L0** — the Lock Screen does not even reveal that the event is about Introductions (D15; C-PRIV-1; S28) |
| Richer disclosure | only by the user's explicit choice; the chooser offers all four levels for Introductions (board 07, `notif-lock-intro-raised`) |
| The ceiling | a ceiling, not a requirement: raised to «إظهار النوع», the acceptance renders L1 (S31); raised to «إظهار المعاينة», it renders its bounded L3 words — still no names (S30; C-PRIV-7) |
| Event projection | a pending **proposal** stops at its own L2 even under an L3 ceiling, because before both accept nothing about the other person may be shown (G2.3) — so it has no content preview to give (S29). This is that event's fact, not an Introductions rule |
| No new rule | nothing names or exposes a person by default; no inventory or marketplace presentation; Introductions still shows presence only, never a count (C-MARK-4) |

Planted defect **D17** restores a universal Introductions ≤ L1 cap; **C-PRIV-6** and C-FG-1 reject it.

Every non-default cell is shown only because a user raised that ceiling.

## 4. Human words in settings (task §10; refinement §6)

«معاينات شاشة القفل» / "Lock Screen previews", one row per subject, each opening a chooser of four ceilings:

| Level | Arabic | English | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | «خاصة جدًا» | Very private | **APPROVED** (refinement §6) |
| L1 | **«إظهار النوع»** | **Show type** | **APPROVED** (refinement §6) — the notification's type / category only; no bounded context, no content |
| L2 | «إظهار السياق» | Show context | **APPROVED** (refinement §6) |
| L3 | «إظهار المعاينة» | Show preview | **APPROVED** (refinement §6) |

The first pass's open label «تنبيه عام» / "General" is withdrawn; planted defect **D18** restores it and **C-COPY-1**
rejects it. Each option says what it shows in one line; the sheet says «هذا حدّ أقصى: قد يُظهر قنديل تفاصيل أقل.» The
Introductions line in settings now says «افتراضيًا، لا تكشف شاشة القفل أن الإشعار عن التعارف.» — true by default, and
honest once the user raises the ceiling.

## 5. Native outside, QANDEEL inside (P3-C / P3-Q)

The outer card is the platform's: board 10 draws grey **schematic** stand-ins for an iOS-like and an Android-like
card and claims no pixel accuracy; the app icon is a placeholder. QANDEEL owns only the words. The platform can still
hide more — iOS "Show Previews" (always / when unlocked / never), Android per-channel Lock Screen visibility, where the
user "always has ultimate control". QANDEEL never relies on the device to hide what its own level must not say.
